questions.question: If a parent asks you to change a bus stop location, what should you do?

options.text: Agree and pick up students at the new location.
Continue picking up students at the original bus stop.
Change the bus stop if it fits your route.
Use both locations as bus stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue picking up students at the original bus stop.
questions.explanation: Only school district officials can change bus stop locations. Bus drivers do not have this authority.

questions.question: During the driving test, when asked to make a turn, what should you do?

options.text: Skip the turn signal since you were told to turn.
Check traffic only to your right.
Check traffic in all directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check traffic in all directions.
questions.explanation: Always check traffic in all directions and use your turn signal when making a turn during the driving test.

questions.question: What tool should you use to check tire inflation?

options.text: A tire gauge
A tire iron
An air compressor
A lug nut

questions.correctAnswerText: A tire gauge
questions.explanation: Use a tire gauge to check tire inflation during the vehicle inspection test. Simply kicking the tires is not acceptable.

questions.question: How should you perform pre-trip inspections?

options.text: Use a different method each time to check different items.
Use the same method each time to avoid forgetting items.
Do them only occasionally.
Have someone other than the driver do them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the same method each time to avoid forgetting items.
questions.explanation: Perform pre-trip inspections the same way every time. This routine helps you remember all important checks.

questions.question: Before leaving a bus stop, what should a driver check?

options.text: That no students are running to catch the bus.
That students have put backpacks in the aisle.
That students have opened the emergency vent.
That students are facing the rear of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: That no students are running to catch the bus.
questions.explanation: Always check that no students are running to catch the bus before pulling away from the stop.

questions.question: What is true about loading and unloading a bus?

options.text: It can be dangerous for passengers.
It should be supervised by someone other than the driver.
It should be done while refueling.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can be dangerous for passengers.
questions.explanation: Passengers may trip when getting on or off the bus. Always warn passengers to watch their step when exiting.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing in a placarded vehicle, you should always:

options.text: Turn on your four-way flashers.
Stop within five feet of the tracks.
Change gears while on the tracks.
Change lanes while on the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers.
questions.explanation: Stop between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest rail. Turn on your four-way flashers while crossing. Never stop, change gears, or change lanes while crossing the tracks.

questions.question: What should properly adjusted outside side mirrors on a school bus allow the driver to see?

options.text: The sides of the school bus
Under the school bus
The front tires touching the ground
Vehicles in front of the bus

questions.correctAnswerText: The sides of the school bus
questions.explanation: Properly adjusted outside side mirrors show the sides of the bus, the rear tires touching the ground, and 200 feet behind the bus.

questions.question: During the driving skills test, you may be asked to recall details after driving over a bridge. What might you be asked?

options.text: The posted weight limit
The color of a sign you passed
How many traffic lanes were on the bridge
Whether there was a crosswalk on the bridge

questions.correctAnswerText: The posted weight limit
questions.explanation: The examiner may ask you to recall the bridge's posted weight limit after you drive over it during the driving test.

questions.question: After stopping during the stop/start maneuver test, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on the four-way flashers.
Don't use flashers because it is just a test, not an emergency.
Leave the vehicle in first gear.
Park in front of a fire hydrant.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on the four-way flashers.
questions.explanation: Once stopped, turn on your four-way flashers and shift into neutral or park. Do not block driveways, intersections, fire hydrants, or signs.

questions.question: When doing a driver's side parallel park, you should:

options.text: Pass the space while backing, then pull forward into it.
Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
Pull forward into the space without passing it first.
Back into the space without passing it first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: You may need to parallel park into a space on your left. Drive past the space first. Then back into it, keeping your rear as close to the rear of the space as possible. Your vehicle must be completely inside the space boundaries.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you will:

options.text: Explain what you know about the inspection process.
Watch someone else check your vehicle.
Watch a video about how to inspect a vehicle.
Change all the tires on your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain what you know about the inspection process.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must do a complete inspection of your vehicle. You need to explain what you are checking and why you are checking it.

questions.question: When the examiner asks you to change lanes during the test, you should:

options.text: Change lanes right away without looking.
Use your turn signal and change lanes when it is safe.
Change lanes as fast as possible, even if you cut off another driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signal and change lanes when it is safe.
questions.explanation: The examiner will ask you to change lanes during the driving test. Check your mirrors and blind spots. Use your turn signal. Only change lanes when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: If a railroad gate does not go back up after a train passes, you should:

options.text: Drive around the gate.
Wait for another vehicle to cross first to see if it is safe.
Call your dispatcher.

questions.correctAnswerText: Call your dispatcher.
questions.explanation: If a gate stays down after a train passes, call your dispatcher right away. Do not try to drive around the lowered gate.

questions.question: During the driving test, the examiner scores you on:

options.text: Your attitude.
How fast you reach your destination.
Your driving behavior overall.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your driving behavior overall.
questions.explanation: The examiner scores you on specific driving moves and your general driving behavior during the on-road driving test.

questions.question: Student safety is best protected by:

options.text: Keeping students on the bus.
Letting some students get off the bus.
Letting students get off and scatter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeping students on the bus.
questions.explanation: In most emergencies, students are safest and easiest to control if they stay on the school bus. Keep students on the bus as long as it does not put them at risk or cause injury.

questions.question: A school bus must be evacuated if:

options.text: The bus breaks down in winter weather.
The air conditioning breaks.
There is danger of a collision.
Students are feeling sick.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is danger of a collision.
questions.explanation: Students should stay on the bus during most emergencies. Evacuate only if the bus is on railroad tracks, the bus is on fire or may catch fire, there is a hazardous materials spill, or there is danger of a collision.

questions.question: When you encounter a railroad crossing during the test, you should:

options.text: Pass another vehicle on the tracks if it is going too slow.
Get out of your vehicle to check for a train.
Not change gears while on the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not change gears while on the tracks.
questions.explanation: During the driving test, do not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on the railroad tracks.

questions.question: If you must drive in high winds, you should:

options.text: Loosen your grip on the steering wheel.
Drive faster.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: A school bus's long sides can be pushed by wind. In windy conditions, grip the steering wheel firmly, watch for wind gusts, and reduce your speed. If needed, call your dispatcher for guidance.

questions.question: When getting out of your vehicle, you should:

options.text: Jump directly from your seat to the ground.
Keep at least one hand on your vehicle.
Face your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Face your vehicle.
questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle during the basic vehicle control skills test, face the vehicle and maintain three points of contact at all times. For a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly may result in automatic failure.
